intro: The smiley face icon is a smiling face drawn inside a rounded square, and in most interfaces it opens an emoji picker or a reaction menu. It invites a quick, friendly response, so you will see it in chat composers, comment boxes and feedback widgets where tone matters more than words.
meaning: The smiling face traces back to the 1960s yellow smiley badge and later to text emoticons typed with a colon and a bracket in early online chat. Today people treat it as an emoji icon: press it and a grid of faces and symbols appears. Placed among other faces, a happy face icon becomes the satisfied option on a rating scale. It differs from the heart or thumbs up, which record one fixed reaction straight away instead of opening a choice.
uses: Chat composer: a button beside the text field that opens the emoji and sticker picker.
Message hover menu: an add reaction control that lets people respond to a message with any emoji.
Post-purchase survey: the happiest option in a row of faces rating the checkout experience.
Profile status editor: a control for choosing an emoji that appears beside your name, like a holiday or busy marker.
tips: The rounded square frame keeps the face from looking like a user avatar; keep it rather than switching to a plain circle in tight spaces.
In rating scales, add text such as Very happy under each face, because expressions read differently across cultures and to screen readers.
Place the emoji picker button on the opposite side from Send, so a mistapped smile never fires off a half-written message.

faq.q: What does the smiley icon in a chat box do?
faq.a: It opens the emoji picker. Tap it and a panel of faces, gestures and symbols appears, and choosing one inserts it into your message. In some apps a smiley with a small plus sign adds a reaction to an existing message instead.

faq.q: Should I use a smiley face or a thumbs up for reactions?
faq.a: Use the smiley face when people should choose from many reactions, since it opens a menu. Use a thumbs up when there is only one quick reaction, such as liking a comment. Many apps show both: the thumbs up for one tap, the smiley for everything else.
